contexts.text: There are also presented to view cities with magnificent palaces, contiguous, resplendent in their colouring, beyond all the art of the architect.

Those who... in the life of the body, had dwelt in magnificent palaces, placing their Heaven in such things, and, being destitute of conscience and charity, had despoiled others of their goods... are sometimes allowed to dwell in palaces, in like manner as in the world... But the scene is changed. The palaces are slowly dissipated, and become small houses, more and more mean, and at last none at all...
Palaces (), or houses, = voluntary things.
Courts = the external things of the Church; and palaces, the internal things.
When this truth inflows into the First Heaven... it appears there... as a City in which are palaces.
He who believes from the heart... that of himself he possesses nothing... in Heaven... dwells in most magnificent palaces. References.
The palace () = the Word, consequently the truth of doctrine which is from good.
Like one who is building a palace...
Around Spirits who are in truths from good, there appear the most beautiful representatives; namely, houses and palaces refulgent with gold and precious stones...
Before the Spirits (of the Third Earth) were represented magnificent palaces... but they held them in no estimation... SE 1681.
Like the prefects, officials, and ministers in one royal palace...

There have been seen palaces of Heaven, which were so magnificent that they cannot be described. Above, they shone as if they were of pure gold; and below as if of precious stones; one palace being more resplendent than another. Within, the rooms were adorned with such decorations as neither words nor knowledges suffice to describe. At the side which looked to the south, there were paradises... At the boundaries again were seen palaces, in which the view terminated.
(The prefects) dwell in the middle of the Society, higher up than the rest, and in magnificent palaces.

They compared the wisdom of the Angels of the Third Heaven to a magnificent palace, full of all things for use... and those Angels, being in the truths of wisdom, can enter into the palace, and see all things...
(Such) cannot come to the first threshold of the palace of wisdom...

Some (of the rich in Heaven) dwell in palaces, within which all things shine as from gold and silver... but they do not set their hearts on these things; but on the uses... Uses themselves are thus refulgent in Heaven... DP 220:10.
In the Spiritual World appear... houses and palaces...

All things which appear there are correspondences... This is why those in the affection of good and truth, and thence in wisdom and intelligence, dwell in magnificent palaces, around which are paradises...
The Angels represent wisdom to themselves as a magnificent and most ornate palace; the ascent to which is by twelve steps...
This universal Providence is seen... by the Lord, as a magnificent palace, with its work of construction and enlargement constantly going on. (See SE 3724.)
A magnificent palace seen, and in its inmost a temple (in which was held a Council of the clergy). BE 120. TCR 188.
In front was a lowly palace...
Those of the highest [rank] in Heaven have palaces and courts, which in magnificence and splendour surpass the palaces and courts of earthly emperors and kings.
I will introduce yon into (the Prince's) palace...

When they were brought to the palace, they first viewed it from without. It was large, built of porphyry, with a substructure of jasper; and before the gate were six lofty columns of lapis lazuli. The roof was of plates of gold; the lofty windows, of the most transparent crystal, also had frames of gold... Within the palace they were conducted from room to room; and saw ornaments of ineffable beauty; on the ceilings, decorations of inimitable carving. Near the walls they saw silver tables overlaid with gold, on which were various utensils made of precious stones, and of entire gems, in heavenly forms... The Angel said. The things you see... were framed by the Maker of the universe, and presented as a gift to our Prince; and here therefore is the architectonic art in its own art... As our hearts are not in these things, they are only accessory to the joys of our hearts...
They were introduced into the court-yard, the ambulatory of the palace...
(In the city of the Silver Age) the houses were so many palaces, built of marble, with steps of alabaster in front; and, at the sides of the steps, columns of jasper...
[151a]. On the top of the hill was an octagonal palace, which they called the Palladium...
All things in that Society... are magnificent from the palaces and paradises.

(The three pairs of birds) flew to a certain lofty palace in the east... In the palace were three rows of windows... That palace represented the habitations of conjugial love in human minds. Explained.
I saw... a portico leading to a small palace. Described.
I saw afar off a palace beset by a crowd...
(When his external sight was opened) he saw magnificent palaces of alabaster, marble, and various precious stones, (which vanished when his internal sight was opened).
He was introduced into one of the palaces. Described.
Like one who from the roof of his palace sees...
There are also (there) things which are called heavenly habitations; namely, magnificent palaces...
The palaces constructed by art in the world are as nothing [in comparison]...
The rich (Dutch) at first seem to themselves to dwell in magnificent palaces (which are gradually changed) into mean houses; and then into none at all.
Like the materials collected for a great palace...
(The palace of those who are in the persuasion that faith alone saves, and yet live mercifully, from conscience). Described.
On the palaces in the other life.
The Angels dwell in palaces so magnificent... and this with variety to eternity.
But where the Angels are, there are the most magnificent palaces, such as cannot be described... They shine with the most precious woods and stones.
Who would believe that (in the Heavens) there are palaces in which they dwell, most magnificent...

I was brought to a great palace like the castle in Stockholm. (Continued. See New Church.) LJPost 116. [NCBS: Here, Swedenborg describes the same experience in similar terms, but without comparing the palace to the one in Stockholm.]
There appeared (in the Heavens) mountains higher and higher, which were still better cultivated, and where there were magnificent palaces.
(Those in the Celestial Kingdom) have palaces, etc.

(In Heaven) they see... also palaces, with decorations varying perpetually, with such harmony, that the successions of the changes occasion inexpressible delight to the lower mind. Within, are rooms in such an order as cannot be described, with stupendous ornaments in them.
Otherwise, he stands far outside the palace of wisdom...
When they arrived, the house was changed into a beautiful palace, with many rooms. (Continued. See Marriage.)
These things the Angels have from correspondence; whence it is that the wiser Angels have palaces more magnificent than the less wise Angels.
The palace shall be a desert () = where good dwells.

Peace be in thy bulwark, and rest in thy palaces () = in the exterior and the interior man; for... the interior man, with the things therein, which are spiritual truths and goods, is like a palace, or house; because it is within the exterior. Hence... the interior things of man are signified by palaces.
Palaces () = the things of doctrine.
That truths are inscribed on those who are in celestial good, is signified by, God is known in her palaces ().
The palace () = the whole Church as to truths from good.
Where the Angels dwell, there are palaces, etc.
To distinguish her palaces () = to perceive the goods of truth. For houses = goods; and palaces, the more noble goods of truth.
Palaces () = all things of thought and affection.
By phantasies, evil Spirits can present palaces, etc.
Palaces = the more interior, and thence the mere sublime things, of the human mind. Hence it is evident what is signified by, death... shall come into our palaces ().
Palaces () = falsities themselves; which are called palaces, because they are proud; and because their falsities are embellished in the external form, so as to appear magnificent...
The dogmas which defend them are signified by palaces and fortifications ().
By her palaces in which are the ijim, and by the temples in which are dragons () are signified the goods and truths of the Word adulterated and profaned.

The affections of truth are compared to corners cut out in the figure of a palace (), because a palace is a representative of the understanding, in which Truths are in a beautiful form; and they are in a beautiful form when they are from the affection of truth.

The palace shall be inhabited, according to its manner () = the spiritual understanding of Truths, as with the Ancients: a palace = the understanding of Spiritual Truths; for in the understanding are spiritual Truths in their forms, which, when presented to view, appear as palaces.
The endeavour to destroy the understanding of truth, is signified by, Let us destroy her palaces ().

In the Spiritual Heaven there are magnificent palaces, within which all things are refulgent with precious stones, and with decorations in such forms that they cannot be imitated by any picture in the world, nor be expressed in words. For art there is in its own art, especially that of architecture.
They shall come into the palace of the king () = with heavenly joy into Heaven, where the Lord is.
Palaces of ivory () = truths from the rational man; thus rational truths.

In the Societies of Heaven there are prefects... Their chief, who is wiser than the rest, dwells in the middle, in a palace so magnificent, that not anything in the universal world can be compared to it. Its architectural features are so stupendous that... not one hundredth part of them can be described in natural language; for art itself is there in its own art. Within the palace there are chambers and bed-chambers, in which all the furniture and ornaments are resplendent with gold and various precious stones, in such forms as cannot be effigied, either by painting or sculpture, by any artificer in the world; and, wonderful to say, each most singular thing is for use; everyone who enters seeing for what use it is; and also perceiving it as if from a transpiration of the uses through their images. But every wise person who enters does not long keep his eye fixed on the images; but he keeps his mind in the uses... Round about the palace there are porticoes, paradisiacal gardens, and little palaces; and every single thing is a heavenly pleasantness in the form of its own beauty.
The abodes of the Mohammedans after death are palaces...
I was brought to the Africans ... and saw there as it were a palace...
In Heaven there are palaces so magnificent that worldly things cannot be compared to them...
5. At the end of the way of wisdom was seen a palace in light; but at the end of the way of folly, something like a palace, but in shade...
